territorial_scope.description: Applies to government entities of the State of Utah as defined in the chapter, including state agencies, legislative and judicial bodies, and political subdivisions.

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Restricts Utah government entities' use of facial recognition systems on image databases to specified law enforcement purposes, bans use for civil immigration violations, requires trained-employee verification, public notice and data-use limits, and annual reporting. Effective date not stated in the provided text.
summary.long: The chapter covers the government entities defined in Section 77-23e-102(5), including state agencies, the Legislature, courts and political subdivisions. Section 77-23e-103 bars government entities from using a facial recognition system on an image database, subject to exceptions in Sections 77-23e-103 to 105. Only law enforcement agencies may request comparisons, in writing; a trained employee may complete them only for listed purposes such as investigating a felony, a violent crime or a threat to human life, with a case number and, for crime investigations, a statement supporting a fair probability of connection. Civil immigration violations are excluded. The Department of Public Safety alone may run comparisons on images it maintains or shares (Section 77-23e-104). Trained employees must use an algorithm comparing only facial biometric data, verify possible matches visually and obtain a second opinion. Entities must notify individuals when capturing images, publish notice at least 30 days before new use, accept public comment for 15 days and post the final decision. Comparison data may not be used or shared beyond the chapter's purposes. Entities release statistics on request and report annually to the Government Operations Interim Committee between August 1 and October 15. The text contains no penalty provisions and no effective date.
